messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PROD runtime-prefetch: sustained p99 latency 4.8s (threshold 2s) in us-west-2 streaming cluster. SLOs impacted. auto-page oncall.
Maya: I'm on it, looking at console -> https://console.redwood/inference/metrics/runtime-prefetch?window=5m
Maya: p95 1.2s, p99 4.8s, streaming stalls showing as 'tail stall' traces in traces view
Maya: Claire + support, any customer reports?
Claire: Yep — two customers (acme-corp, demo-inc) reported timeouts for streaming chat. CS is triaging and collecting logs.
Maya: checking cache hit rates: prefixcache hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~11% in the last 8-10m for us-west-2 shards
Maya: suspect recent prefix-hash rollout (v3) caused key mismatch / invalidation
Sean: I rolled prefix-hash v3 to 25% canary at 00:45Z. No alerts during canary window initially.
Maya: spike started ~00:50Z and correlates with canary ramp to more nodes
Amir: @Maya paste last 100 log lines with "invalid-prefix" or "prefix-lookup miss"
Maya: logs:
```
[00:51:02] shard-12 WARN prefix-lookup miss key=usr_1234 prefix_hash=7f3a expected=5c2b
[00:51:03] runtime: stream stall waiting for kvfetch shard=12 latency=3100ms
[00:51:04] cache: insert failed namespace=prefix-v3 err=invalid-prefix-salt
[00:51:05] proxy: fallback read prefix-v2 succeeded for key=usr_1234
```
Maya: rolling the canary back now -> running rollback command
Maya: `infractl rollout revert prefixhash v3 --env prod --percent 0` -> submitted, targeting all nodes
OpsBot: rollback job started (job id job-8791). Estimated 2m to complete.
Maya: also enabling temporary routing fallback to prefix-v2: `routingctl set fallback prefix-v2` (immediate)
Sean: good. I'm watching p99 and stream success rate. If rollback doesn't fix within 3m, we'll open emergency path (route to dedicated cache tier).
Claire: I'm drafting an interim customer note: "We're investigating intermittent streaming delays for a subset of customers; mitigation in progress." Will post once rollback confirmed :thumbsup:.
OpsBot: rollback job job-8791 completed successfully
Maya: rollback confirmed. prefixcache hit-rate recovering: 11% -> 74% in ~90s for affected shards
Maya: p99 back down to ~1.9s, p95 ~0.9s. Streaming stalls dropped to baseline.
Claire: Message posted to customers, flagged for follow-up. No elevated escalations yet.
Amir: For RCA candidate: the v3 prefix-salt algorithm changed key salt leading to cache key namespace split. Keys were not rehashed; reads were falling through to KV backend causing high tail latency.
Maya: opened incident ticket: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026 (S2)
Maya: proposed next steps: 1) Pause v3 rollout immediately (done). 2) Implement dual-read mode (v2 + v3) for 24h to allow warm-up. 3) Build migration job to rehash and copy hot keys OR a background rewriter. 4) Add telemetry alert: if prefixcache hit-rate drops >20 percentage points in 5m, auto-pause rollouts.
Sean: +1 on dual-read as low-risk. I'll prototype dual-read logic and measure overhead. Aim to have a canary-safe approach by EOD.
Maya: also adding a short-term cache-ttl bump on affected shards to reduce backend load while we stabilize.
Amir: please add affected shard list and customers to the incident ticket. Claire, ensure CS has the precise customer list and timestamp windows.
Claire: done. Added acme-corp, demo-inc, and a couple of trial accounts. Sending scoped emails now.
Maya: Handoff: I'm leaving in ~30m. Handing this to Amir for overnight monitoring and RCA ownership.
Amir: Taking over. Will continue monitoring dashboards and coordinate postmortem. I'll schedule a quick sync in 2h for engineers working on the dual-read/migration.
Maya: thanks everyone. Closing live mitigation notes here; moving to post-incident follow-up.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 created, severity S2. Postmortem requested within 72h.
